stories.label: Donald Trump to send US officials to Pakistan for fresh peace talks with Iran
stories.summary: Trump sends negotiators to Islamabad Tuesday for a second round of US-Iran ceasefire talks — with Pakistan as the mediator and Trump threatening 'no more Mr. Nice Guy.' Lead with Pakistan's unusual broker role: a Muslim nuclear state staging talks between the US and Iran after March drone strikes in the Gulf. Source sentiment diverges sharply (Dawn +0.11 to Times of Israel -0.43), so the zuhd take is the mechanism — Islamabad gains leverage, Tehran signals it will 'stand to the end,' and the ceasefire hinges on whether Washington keeps power-plant targeting on the table.

stories.label: Spain urges EU to scrap Association Agreement with Israel
stories.summary: PM Sánchez gave the EU 48 hours to suspend its trade and political framework with Israel, citing violations of international law. Lead with the mechanism — the Association Agreement governs preferential tariffs, research funding, and political dialogue; scrapping it would be the EU's sharpest economic lever against Israel since the Gaza war began. Multi-source sentiment spread (0.11 to -0.30 across FR/IL/TR/MY/IN) captures the split: European enforcement of EU human-rights clauses vs. an Israeli government calling the push illegitimate. Accountability angle: will Brussels act, or defer to the Council where Germany and Hungary block?

stories.label: Eight children killed in Louisiana shooting
stories.summary: Eight children aged 1-14 killed in a Shreveport, Louisiana mass shooting — one of the deadliest child-targeting attacks in recent US history. Lead with the ages and name the victims when available; dignity demands the dead are counted individually, not aggregated as 'eight'. Structural angle: Louisiana has some of the weakest firearm laws in the US and preempts local gun ordinances, so the policy failure is state-level, not federal. Avoid the motive-hunt frame — report what is known and who was lost.

stories.label: US diplomat says attacks on Iranian power plants will not be war crime
stories.summary: US UN envoy Michael Waltz publicly argues that strikes on Iranian power plants would not constitute war crimes — a legal stance that pre-authorizes targeting civilian electricity infrastructure in ongoing negotiations. Lead with the precedent: the same logic was used to justify power-grid strikes in Iraq 1991 and Serbia 1999, both later cited by ICRC and HRW as causing disproportionate civilian harm. Accountability angle: a sitting US official is narrating the legal cover for future attacks in the middle of a ceasefire track (see Trump-Pakistan talks story). Note this is a single-source TASS story — writer should corroborate Waltz's exact wording before publishing.

stories.label: Sayed Moshagheb rearrested hours after release from 11 years imprisonment
stories.summary: Egyptian activist Sayed Moshagheb was rearrested within hours of completing an 11-year sentence — the 'rotation' tactic Egypt uses to keep political prisoners detained indefinitely by opening a new case before release paperwork clears. Lead with the mechanism: the case file is recycled with fresh charges, restarting pre-trial detention clocks. Accountability angle: this is a documented pattern (HRW and EIPR have cataloged it), and Sisi's government deploys it systematically against journalists, lawyers, and Muslim Brotherhood-linked figures. Name the prosecutor's office if sources allow.

stories.label: India cautiously unlocks Chinese investment after years of resistance
stories.summary: India is quietly relaxing the 2020 FDI curbs that required government approval for any Chinese investment — originally imposed after the Galwan border clash. Lead with the specific policy shift (approvals now routed via a fast-track channel for non-strategic sectors) and the number: Chinese FDI applications pending since 2020 cleared ~$2bn worth this quarter. Why now: India's electronics and EV assembly lines need Chinese components, and Modi's government has concluded that the self-reliance rhetoric has cost manufacturing more than it gained. Structural angle for the ummah: an Asian rival-to-rival thaw reshapes supply chains that touch Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Gulf. Single-source think-tank piece — writer should confirm the FDI-route specifics against India's DPIIT notifications.

stories.label: Pakistan in discussion with Qatar for supply of LNG cargoes amid electricity shortfall
stories.summary: Islamabad is negotiating fresh Qatari LNG cargoes as power generation falters heading into summer peak demand. Lead with the shortage number and what it means for load-shedding hours. Structural angle: Pakistan's LNG reliance is a post-2022 European-price-shock story — when Europe outbid Asian buyers for cargoes, Pakistan was cut off and forced into costly spot-market purchases, fueling the 2023 IMF package. The Qatar route is cheaper and diplomatically cleaner, but ties Pakistan's grid stability to a single Gulf supplier just as Strait of Hormuz tensions (see Trump-Iran story) threaten LNG shipping lanes.

stories.label: Antitrust Authority Approves Creation of Rheinmetall-OHB Satellite Joint Venture
stories.summary: Germany's BKartA cleared a Rheinmetall-OHB satellite JV, consolidating Europe's sovereign military-satellite capacity under a defense contractor (Rheinmetall) rather than a pure space firm. Lead with who is being locked out: SpaceX and Airbus Defence lose the default-European-ISR position, and the JV positions Berlin to field its own reconnaissance constellation by 2028. Structural angle: this is Europe's answer to the US-dependency problem exposed by the Starlink-Ukraine controversy — satellite intelligence is being re-nationalized through defense-industrial consolidation. Accountability angle: note the combined shareholder structure and whether civilian-science launches will be crowded out of OHB's backlog.

stories.label: Theoretical models of supernova chemistry overhauled after X-ray data from Perseus Cluster reveal key discrepancies
stories.summary: X-ray spectra from the Perseus Cluster show element abundances (chromium, manganese, nickel) that standard Type-Ia supernova models can't produce — forcing a rethink of how heavy elements get into the interstellar medium. Lead with the concrete discrepancy (observed vs. predicted ratios) and which telescope (XRISM / Chandra) delivered the data. Why it matters: supernova yields calibrate how we estimate galactic chemical evolution — if the models are off, so are age estimates for stars and constraints on dark-matter halos. Teach the mechanism: the white-dwarf detonation channel vs. the deflagration-to-detonation transition.

stories.label: These blazing blue explosions may be born when a compact dead star slams into a Wolf-Rayet star
stories.summary: Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transients (LFBOTs) — rare, extremely hot explosions that fade in days — may come from a neutron star or black hole plowing into a Wolf-Rayet companion. Lead with the candidate mechanism and why it explains what supernovae can't: the fast fade, the blue color, the X-ray signature. Teach the physics: Wolf-Rayet stars have blown off their hydrogen envelopes, so a compact companion inspiralling into their dense cores produces a violent but short-lived burst. Avoid the 'cosmic mystery' frame — name the competing hypotheses (failed supernova, intermediate-mass black hole tidal disruption) the new model rules out.

stories.label: Why Japan has such good railways
stories.summary: Japan's rail quality comes from a specific institutional design: private operators own the track *and* the property around stations, so profits from real-estate capture fund train reliability. Lead with the mechanism — vertical integration of rail + land — and contrast with US/UK franchise models where track and operations are split. Teach the reader why privatization 'works' here and fails elsewhere: the unit of ownership is the corridor, not the train service. Structural angle: countries now copying Japan's TOD (Transit-Oriented Development) model — Indonesia's Jakarta MRT, Pakistan's Karachi Circular Railway revival — inherit the financing logic, not just the trains. Feature-length essay but analytically dense; writer should distill to the mechanism and name 2-3 concrete policy levers.

stories.label: AI warfare triggers Putin, as Kremlin moves to dismantle the last pieces of Russian internet
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] Telegram is blocked, VPNs are being chased after, but Putin suddenly talks about a national AI again.

stories.label: FAA Scraps Civil and Criminal Penalties for Flying Drones Near ICE Vehicles
stories.summary: The FAA rolled back civil and criminal penalties for flying drones near ICE vehicles — but the government retains the right to shoot drones down and has expanded the list of protected agencies to include DOJ. Lead with the legal asymmetry: filming is now legal, but the aircraft can still be destroyed without recourse. Structural: press-freedom and accountability-journalism stakes when the target of filming is also the authority regulating airspace.

stories.label: Fire razes 200 homes in Sabah, leaving hundreds homeless
stories.summary: Fire destroyed about 200 homes in Sandakan, displacing over 9,000 people — many stateless or undocumented Bajau Laut and Suluk in stilt-house villages. Lead with who the displaced actually are: a population that Malaysia's own bureaucracy renders invisible, now homeless without papers to access aid.

stories.label: Traffic restored on Karakoram Highway following landslide as heavy rainfall lashes GB
stories.summary: Heavy April rain triggered landslides that severed the Karakoram Highway, Gilgit-Baltistan's only land link to the rest of Pakistan and to China. Lead with the chokepoint: a single road carries CPEC trade and food/fuel for 1.5 million people in GB. Frame as climate-fragility on a strategic corridor.

stories.label: Is the world facing a food crisis?
stories.summary: Daily Maverick traces converging shocks — climate, fertilizer prices since the Russia/Ukraine war, the Iran-US war's effect on shipping — pushing global food import bills to record highs. Lead with the mechanism: it's not a single failed harvest, it's the compounding of disrupted inputs that hits import-dependent African and Asian states first.

stories.label: Painkiller Pipeline: 300 Million Tapentadol Pills Sent from India to West Africa
stories.summary: Bellingcat traced 300 million tapentadol pills shipped from a single Indian manufacturer, Aveo, into West Africa over two years — an opioid not approved for sale in those markets, fueling addiction crises across Ghana, Nigeria, and Côte d.Ivoire. Lead with the supply chain: India's lax export controls, fake destination paperwork, and West African ports overwhelmed. Names the manufacturer and the regulatory gap.

stories.label: Sudan Nashra: Dengue outbreak in Khartoum, medical sources say capital still unprepared | Measles outbreak causes daily deaths in North Darfur displacement hubs | Mahamid RSF commander, forces defect to the military | RSF-SPLM-N shelling kills 6 in Dalang, military foils new offensive
stories.summary: Mada Masr's weekly Sudan brief: dengue outbreak in Khartoum the capital cannot treat, daily measles deaths in North Darfur displacement hubs, and an RSF commander defecting to the army. Lead with the epidemiology: a war that has destroyed health infrastructure now compounds with mosquito- and vaccine-preventable disease in displaced populations. The defection signals RSF cohesion fraying.

stories.label: Ransomware attack continues to disrupt healthcare in London nearly two years later
stories.summary: Synnovis ransomware attack on London NHS pathology — June 2024 — is still degrading services nearly two years on; thousands of operations rescheduled and a patient death linked to the disruption. Lead with the duration: ransomware against critical infrastructure is not an event, it is a chronic condition the NHS still has not recovered from. Names the vendor concentration risk.

stories.label: Quantum ‘Jamming’ Explores the Truly Fundamental Principles of Nature
stories.summary: Quanta on a new theoretical framework using 'jamming' — the physics of how granular materials lock up — as a fundamental principle behind phase transitions, neural-network learning, and even cosmology. Lead with the unification: the same math that describes a sandpile collapse may describe how complex systems organize. For technically literate readers, this is a worldview-shifting concept piece.

stories.label: DeBriefed 17 April 2026: Fossil-fuel power slumps | ‘Super’ El Niño warning | Afghanistan’s climate struggle
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's weekly: global fossil-fuel power generation hit a record decline in Q1, NOAA warns of a possible 'super' El Niño returning in late 2026, and Afghanistan's drought-and-floods cycle worsens with no climate finance reaching the Taliban-governed state. Lead with the fossil-power slump number — it's the first clear sign that wind+solar growth has overtaken demand growth globally.

stories.label: Bangladesh’s gig workers are stuck in gas lines as Iran-U.S. war strains fuel supply
stories.summary: Iran-US war disrupted Persian Gulf fuel exports; Bangladesh's CNG stations now ration, leaving Pathao and Uber gig drivers queuing 4-6 hours per shift. Lead with the wage collapse: drivers earning $4-6 a day now lose half their shift to the queue. The war 5,000km away has made gig work in Dhaka unviable. Concrete consequence story.

stories.label: Kazakhstan has a new constitution. What’s next?
stories.summary: Tokayev's constitutional rewrite removed the clause restricting any one party's parliamentary share, formally ending the 'managed democracy' framework Nazarbayev built. Lead with what changes in practice: super-presidential powers retained, but the electoral architecture now permits genuine multi-party competition for the first time. Frame as Central Asia's most consequential institutional shift since 1991 — and ask whether the opening is real.

stories.label: Iran war: Tehran says 'progress' made in talks with US
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf claims 'progress' in US talks while Deputy FM Khatibzadeh publicly rejects Trump's demand that Tehran hand over enriched uranium. Lead with the gap: the 'progress' Iran cites excludes the one concession Washington says is non-negotiable. Frame as a stalemate dressed as momentum. Compare sentiment across IL/DE/IN sources — divergence 0.33 shows coverage is already splitting. Relevant for readers tracking what a durable Iran-US deal would actually require.

stories.label: Strait of Hormuz is open, but economic pain is just beginning
stories.summary: At the IMF spring meetings, Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan warned markets are 'too optimistic' about Hormuz reopening: seaborne trade won't approach prewar levels until end of June, and Ras Laffan LNG components could take four years to replace. Lead with the $58B infrastructure damage estimate and the downstream chain — fertilizer, helium for semiconductors, ethylene glycol. The 'war ends, prices settle' reflex is wrong; physical supply chains don't respect diplomatic timelines. Reader gets the economics of stuff-and-distance.

stories.label: The Destroyed Remnants of a Lost World Are Falling to Earth, Scientists Discover
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] A rare class of meteorites called angrites likely come from a strange protoplanet that was catastrophically destroyed in the early solar system, leaving only fragmentary remnants.

stories.label: Babies Born from Dead Parents Will Increase with New Tech. Are We Ready?
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] Reproductive technologies have enabled children to be posthumously conceived from the frozen eggs and sperm of deceased parents, raising legal, ethical, and practical questions.

stories.label: The Iran War Is Hurting Refugees Across the Region
stories.summary: A new report finds the Iran war triggered cascading humanitarian crises that exceeded worst-case projections — Afghan refugees in Iran, Iraqi Kurds displaced by IRGC operations, Pakistani returnees stranded at borders. Lead with the report's numbers versus the pre-war projections, then name the populations bearing the cost of a war declared elsewhere. Follows our ongoing Iran-war arc with a humanitarian frame, not a military one.

stories.label: Strait of Hormuz Is Open, But Economic Pain Is Just Beginning
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait 'completely open' ahead of US talks in Pakistan; oil prices tumbled — but insurance premiums, shipping reroutes, and LNG contract repricing from the closure period will take months to unwind. Lead with the gap between headline oil price and the sticky costs: war-risk insurance, tanker chartering, Gulf port throughput. Continues our Hormuz arc with the economic-aftermath angle we haven't covered.

stories.label: Victoria to Extend Free Public Transport for Millions
stories.summary: The Australian state of Victoria extends free public transport for another month and half-price fares for the rest of 2026 — one of the largest farebox-revenue forgone experiments in the developed world. Lead with the fiscal cost and ridership impact so far; structural story is whether free transit scales or becomes a political ratchet that can't be unwound. Useful contrast for readers watching transit-funding debates globally.

stories.label: Why Michael Saylor's Strategy Decided to Make STRC's Dividend Bi-Monthly
stories.summary: Strategy (MSTR) is splitting its STRC perpetual preferred dividend into bi-monthly payments to keep the stock trading closer to par — a technical tell that the bitcoin-treasury-company financial engineering is running into liquidity mechanics. Lead with what bi-monthly actually means for holders, then the broader point: the bitcoin-treasury trade depends on preferred-equity plumbing that's now being adjusted in real time. For readers tracking crypto-finance structure.

stories.label: ESA's Mars Rover to Launch Aboard SpaceX Falcon Heavy in 2028
stories.summary: NASA selected SpaceX Falcon Heavy to launch the ESA Rosalind Franklin Mars rover in late 2028 — the same rover that was stranded when Russia's Proton launch was cancelled after the 2022 invasion. Lead with the geopolitical arc: a European life-seeking mission that lost its Russian ride, waited six years, and now goes up on an American commercial rocket. Structural: European space autonomy is a fiction; launch capacity is an American commercial monopoly.

stories.label: AI is about to make the global e-waste crisis much worse
stories.summary: AI's GPU refresh cycle is vastly shorter than the CPU-era enterprise cycle — hyperscalers retire accelerators in 3-4 years instead of 7-10, and most of them flow to informal e-waste markets in Ghana, Pakistan, and Indonesia. Lead with the specific GPU volume projection and which countries absorb the waste. The structural angle: the Global South pays the material cost of wealthy-country AI buildouts, recovered copper and gold aside, in lead and cadmium groundwater contamination. Connects to accountability on corporate environmental externalisation.

stories.label: 12 countries, including Pakistan, condemn Israel's move to appoint envoy to Somaliland
stories.summary: Twelve states issued a joint statement condemning Israel's appointment of a diplomatic representative to Somaliland — a move that effectively recognises the breakaway region without Mogadishu's consent. Lead with the named signatories and the precedent: Israel using Horn-of-Africa diplomacy to outflank an Arab/OIC consensus on Somali sovereignty. Tie to the broader pattern of Israel cultivating ties with secessionist or unrecognised polities. The mechanism to highlight is the use of recognition as foreign-policy leverage.

stories.label: India summons Iran ambassador after gunboats fire on Indian-flagged tankers in Hormuz
stories.summary: India's MEA summoned Iran's ambassador after Iranian gunboats fired on two Indian-flagged ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with the diplomatic break — India has spent the war as one of Tehran's quietest defenders, buying discounted crude and resisting US pressure; firing on its tankers shifts that calculus. Use the Newsweek-recorded captain audio ('let me turn back') to ground the scene, then triangulate with the Haaretz/Israeli framing of Iranian escalation. The mechanism: how Iran's tactical pressure on Hormuz shipping costs it its most important non-aligned partner.

stories.label: From smelters to servers: Alcoa to sell idle aluminum smelter to bitcoin firm NYDIG
stories.summary: Alcoa is selling its idle Massena East smelter in upstate New York to bitcoin firm NYDIG — the second time in months a US aluminum site has converted to crypto/AI compute, after TeraWulf bought Century Aluminum's Kentucky plant. Lead with the substitution: cheap hydroelectric power that once made primary aluminum is now competitive only as compute. The mechanism to highlight is industrial strategy by default — energy assets the US no longer uses for materials are flowing to digital infrastructure, with implications for re-shoring metals and grid demand.

stories.label: Italian deputy PM Salvini calls for return to Russian gas to avoid 'energy lockdown'
stories.summary: Italy's deputy PM and League leader Matteo Salvini publicly called for Rome to resume Russian gas purchases, framing the Iran-war supply shock as proof Europe's pivot to LNG and North African gas was premature. Lead with the political crack inside the EU sanctions consensus — a sitting deputy PM, not a backbencher. Note that TASS is the source, so verification posture matters: report Salvini's call as fact (he has made similar statements before), but flag the Russian-state framing. The mechanism: how energy prices, not diplomacy, dictate the half-life of European sanctions.

stories.label: DESI completes planned 3D map of the universe and continues exploring
stories.summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument finished the largest high-resolution 3D map of the universe ever made, with 5,000 fibre-optic sensors logging their final scheduled observations near the Little Dipper. Lead with the scale (millions of galaxies, 11 billion years of cosmic history) and what DESI's data has already shown — hints that dark energy may be weakening over time, contradicting the standard cosmological model. The mechanism to highlight is precision spectroscopy as cosmology's new microscope: a single instrument may be forcing a rewrite of our model of the universe.

stories.label: Salty drinking water could be increasing your blood pressure — coastal communities most at risk
stories.summary: New research links elevated sodium in drinking water — driven by saltwater intrusion as sea levels rise — to chronic hypertension in coastal populations. Lead with the human geography: communities in the Bangladeshi delta, the Mekong, Florida, the Nile delta drink water that quietly raises their blood pressure for decades. The mechanism to highlight is climate-as-health-burden by stealth: not a flood, not a storm, just creeping salinity that public-health systems don't measure. This is a justice angle as much as a science one — the populations affected are overwhelmingly in the Global South.

stories.label: Q&A: What Magyar's defeat of Orbán in Hungary means for climate and energy
stories.summary: Péter Magyar's landslide over Viktor Orbán removes one of the EU's most reliable veto players on climate legislation. Lead with what changes inside the European Council: 15 years of Hungarian blocking of bloc-wide climate finance, gas-pipeline reviews, and Russia-energy decoupling now end. The mechanism to highlight is unanimity politics — a single national election can unblock years of stalled EU policy. Note Hungary's lingering Paks II nuclear deal with Rosatom and what Magyar has signalled about it.

stories.label: AI is about to make the global e-waste crisis much worse
stories.summary: As AI hardware demand explodes, the next generation of GPU-class waste will overwhelmingly be dumped, dismantled, and burned in non-Western countries — Ghana's Agbogbloshie, India's Seelampur, Pakistan's Karachi. Lead with the volume and geography: how much e-waste the AI build-out will produce in the next 5 years and which informal recycling economies will absorb it. The mechanism to highlight is regulatory offshoring — the EU's WEEE directive and US state laws push the cost of disposal onto countries with no enforcement capacity. The accountability angle: hyperscalers' net-zero claims rarely include downstream e-waste.

stories.label: Prosecutor general confirms Kyiv shooter was Moscow-born
stories.summary: Ukrainian prosecutor general names the supermarket gunman who killed five Kyiv civilians as Moscow-born — a rare explicit link between a domestic mass-casualty attack and Russian-origin perpetrator. Lead with the named victim toll and the prosecutor's confirmation, then the significance for how Ukraine frames internal security during wartime. 262 sources covered this; pick the detail (Holosiivskyi district supermarket, hostages, police shoot-out) rather than the geopolitical spin.

stories.label: French soldier serving with UNIFIL killed in Lebanon attack
stories.summary: First French UNIFIL fatality in southern Lebanon since the ceasefire; Macron publicly blames Hezbollah. The mechanism to lead with: a 'ceasefire' that continues to produce UN peacekeeper deaths exposes how fragile Lebanon's security arrangement really is, and how little control the Lebanese state has over the contested south. Name the soldier, the location, and the ambush pattern — not just the diplomatic reaction.

stories.label: Israel kills two Gaza water truck drivers - UNICEF
stories.summary: UNICEF publicly condemns Israeli forces for killing two Gaza water truck drivers — humanitarian workers delivering water, not combatants. Lead with the named, specific act and UNICEF's own language. The mechanism: attacks on water distribution are collective punishment under international humanitarian law, and the siege continues to kill through thirst even when cameras are elsewhere. This is an accountability story — name the agency making the charge and what IHL says about targeting aid workers.

stories.label: Blaze Erupts at Russia's Baltic Port After Ukraine Drone Attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones hit a Baltic oil export terminal — deep inside Russia, far from the Black Sea front. Lead with which port and what product (crude or refined) flows through it, because that determines the revenue hit to the Kremlin. The mechanism: Ukraine is systematically degrading Russia's hard-currency earning infrastructure, not just its front-line logistics. Pair with oil-price reaction if any.

stories.label: Six Are Missing After Cargo Ship Is Found Overturned Near Guam
stories.summary: A cargo ship was found overturned near Guam after Super Typhoon Sinklau; six crew missing. Lead with the vessel, the crew nationalities, and the typhoon's intensity. The structural angle: Pacific shipping lanes face escalating typhoon hazard as warmer seas produce more Cat-5 storms, and Guam's Coast Guard SAR capacity is stretched. Keep the missing crew — usually Filipino or Southeast Asian seafarers — at the center, not the ship.

stories.label: How poison frogs built a chemical weapons system one evolutionary step at a time
stories.summary: New research reconstructs the stepwise evolution of poison-frog alkaloid defenses — not one mutation but a sequence of changes in diet, sequestration, and membrane resistance that had to arrive in the right order. Lead with the specific alkaloid and the order of evolutionary steps. The concept for the reader: complex traits that look 'designed' emerge through incremental co-adaptation — a textbook case of how biochemistry and ecology evolve together.

stories.label: Quantum 'Jamming' Explores the Truly Fundamental Principles of Nature
stories.summary: Physicists apply the classical 'jamming transition' — how sand grains suddenly lock into a rigid solid — to quantum systems, revealing universal behaviour at the edge of many-body localisation. Lead with the analogy that grounds the reader (traffic/sand) then the quantum twist. The mechanism worth explaining: jamming is a phase transition without symmetry breaking, and finding quantum analogues sharpens the line between thermodynamic and information-theoretic phases.

stories.label: Babies Born from Dead Parents Will Increase with New Tech. Are We Ready?
stories.summary: Posthumous gamete retrieval is accelerating as cryopreservation improves and courts rule in favor of grieving families — producing children whose legal parents died before conception. Lead with the scale (how many cases annually, trend) and then the unresolved question: consent. The mechanism: tissue extraction 24-72 hours post-mortem, often authorized by spouse or parent, not the deceased. For a Muslim reader, raise the Islamic bioethics angle (nasab, maḥram relations, inheritance) without resolving it — let the reader think.
